newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK TO HIKE MAIN RATE TO 5.70 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK TO HIKE MAIN RATE TO 5.70 PCT.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) will raise its main lev interest rate to 5.70 percent annually from 5.59 percent, effective Monday, dealers said on Thursday.
"The central bank informed us that it will set its main rate at 5.70 percent annually from Monday," a commercial bank dealer told Reuters.
Central bank officials were not immediately avaliable for comment.
The rate rise would be the third in the main rate in as many weeks. Three weeks ago, the rate was at 5.42 percent.

Under a memorandum of economic policy agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March, the BNB adjusts the main interest rate weekly to the yield on three-month discount government securities.
Yield to maturity on the paper was 1.42 percent at Monday's auction, up from 1.40 percent at the last regular auction a week earlier.

The main rate has been declining since March when Bulgaria sealed a 14-month $510 million standby agreement with the IMF and financial stabilisation began taking hold. The rate stood at 18 percent monthly in March.

Bulgaria introduced a fixed-exchange rate regime known as a currency board on July 1 to restore confidence in the financial system and the lev. The lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark, which is used as the anchor currency. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
